groups.title: About this test

blocks.p: Every question of the Text tab gets one more option after its five answers: F, “I don't know”, written in Turkish in the prompt (“Bilmiyorum”). It is always the last option, it is never shuffled and it is never correct. The System One instructions get one added sentence: “If you do not know the answer, choose Bilmiyorum.” A chat model's instructions end with its own sentence instead: “Cevabı bilmiyorsanız Bilmiyorum seçeneğini seçin.” Everything else is as on the Text tab: the same 2,198 scored questions and answer key, and each model's own settings from its text run, its questions per request too (one for every decision model).

The models: the ten most accurate decision models on the Text tab at results 25290875, plus Base Labs' Elephant-1 and Mammoth-1 and SubQ Snap 1.1 once their text runs are published. With them, every chat model setup of the Text tab as its run finishes: 64 so far, one still running in Turkish. Each has one full run; a model whose repeated text runs changed answers gets five.
Download: results.json (every number on this page, under dont_know) and answers.json (each run's record and its outcome on each question, under dont_know_runs).

blocks.p: Of the 67 models, 42 used “I don't know”, on 1.0% to 94.2% of the questions. The other 25, Turion Jev 31B · DGX Spark, Gemini Decision 1 · 20261111, StartLux-Decision-v1.1-4B-Instant, Open-Jev-27B-v1.1, d3-ultra, Copernicus-31B, Adjudex 9B v5, Metask-Jev-4B, Perplexity Decider 27B v1.3, Karpo Decision 31B, KnowLine-9B-Gen1, Verdin-4B-v1.1, REAX 1.3, Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 · API, Logits Sigma-1 Duo, Drex Max, Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 · DGX Spark, KnowLine-31B-Gen1.5 · DGX Spark, Cerno 9B v1.2, KnowLine-12B-Gen1, OneJev-27B, Valen-Decision-1.5-9B, KnowLine-31B-Gen2, Sieve 31B v3 · DGX Spark and d3, chose it on 0 to 21 questions, although each gave it some probability: a mean of 0.2% to 12.7%, against 2.7% to 39.1% for the 42.

GLiDE 0.4B had the highest non-hallucination rate, 95.3%: of its 2,171 answers that were not right, 2,070 were “I don't know”. It answered 5.8% of the questions, with an error rate of 78.9% among those answers. d1.2-ultra (87.3%) and d1.2 (79.4%) follow. With the option, the 42 were less accurate than in their five-option runs on the Text tab, by 0.6 points (Jeffan-9B-1211) to 21.0 points (GLiDE 0.4B: 22.2% against 1.2%). The 25 that almost never chose it moved by -1.0 to +0.9 points.

For 36 of the 42, the model's own confidence on its five-option run, holding back on as many questions (for Laya, 537 against 536: tied scores at the cut-off allow no nearer count), left fewer wrong answers than “I don't know” did: 1 to 40 fewer, a non-hallucination rate 0.0 to 3.6 points higher (the derived rate in the table). d1-Omni-2B, GLiDE · API, GLiDE 0.8B, Microsoft-Decision-1.1, StartLux-Decision-v1.1-0.8B-Instant and KnowLine-0.8B-Gen1 were the exceptions, with 3, 21, 19, 8, 5 and 1 more. groups.title: Our method

blocks.p: We measure hallucination by offering a way out. Every question gets “I don't know” as a sixth option, and the instructions tell the model to choose it when it does not know the answer. A hallucination is then a wrong answer: the model chose one of the question's own options, not the key, when it could have said it did not know. Everything else is the Text tab's: the questions, the answer key and each model's settings.

blocks.h: How it differs from our confidence method

blocks.p: On the Text tab a model must pick one of the five options, and we judge each answer by its confidence: the probability the model gives the option it picked (its option score), or for a chat model the confidence it states. A chat model asked for a plain answer line (Qwen3.5-4B · reasoning on · chat, Gemma 4 E4B · default reasoning · chat, SenseNova-Loop-9B · reasoning on · chat · sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B@3e1ba6e8ac98090f9f7c03a55f26269eb3850fb6, Qwen3.5-4B · reasoning off · chat, LFM2.5-2.6B · default reasoning · chat, Qwen3.5-2B · reasoning off · chat, LFM3-1.7B · reasoning on · chat, LFM3-1.7B · reasoning off · chat, LFM2.5-8B-A1B · default reasoning · chat and MiniCPM5-2B · reasoning off · chat) states none, so its derived rate is not measured. Our confidence method keeps an answer when that confidence reaches a cut-off, and a stronger model answers the rest (How we chose which answers to keep). Here no cut-off decides: the model can say itself that it does not know, by choosing “I don't know”, and the rates count those choices. The two meet in the derived non-hallucination rate, which applies the confidence method to the same model's five-option run at about the same attempt rate; side by side, the two non-hallucination columns compare a model that says it does not know with the same model held back by its own confidence.
Each answer is right, wrong, “I don't know” or invalid; an invalid answer counts as none of the others. Out of all 2,198 questions:

blocks.li: Answered (the attempt rate) = (right + wrong) / 2,198: how often the model chose one of the question's own options.
Error rate = wrong / (right + wrong): among the answers the model gave, the share that were wrong. With no answer it is undefined.

Non-hallucination rate = “I don't know” / (“I don't know” + wrong): among the answers that were wrong or “I don't know”, the share where the model said it did not know. The hallucination rate is its complement, wrong / (“I don't know” + wrong).

Mean probability of “I don't know”: the probability the model gave that option, averaged over its answers that report option probabilities. A chat model states a confidence and reports no option probabilities. A chat model asked for a plain answer line reports neither: not measured.

blocks.p: The non-hallucination rate says how a model is wrong, not how often it is right, and it is not a direct measure of what the model does not know. Read it with accuracy and the attempt rate: a model that always chose “I don't know” would reach 100% with no right answers, and one that never chose it would reach 0% as soon as it answered one question wrongly. With neither a wrong answer nor “I don't know”, there is nothing to divide by and the rate is undefined (the table shows Undefined).
The added option's exact text in the prompt is “Bilmiyorum”. It is lettered after the question's own options, and the answer key is unchanged. The full System One instructions of a decision model:
Which option is the correct answer to this Turkish multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose Bilmiyorum.
Prompt version 1cdd542b597f (a hash of the prompts with these instructions and this option, computed as for the Text tab's prompt version).

A chat model asked for a plain answer line (Qwen3.5-4B · reasoning on · chat, Gemma 4 E4B · default reasoning · chat, SenseNova-Loop-9B · reasoning on · chat · sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B@3e1ba6e8ac98090f9f7c03a55f26269eb3850fb6, Qwen3.5-4B · reasoning off · chat, LFM2.5-2.6B · default reasoning · chat, Qwen3.5-2B · reasoning off · chat, LFM3-1.7B · reasoning on · chat, LFM3-1.7B · reasoning off · chat, LFM2.5-8B-A1B · default reasoning · chat and MiniCPM5-2B · reasoning off · chat) is asked as on the Text tab: one question per request, a user message with one instruction and the question, no system prompt and no answer schema, its answer the letter on the reply's last “CEVAP: X” line. With the option, F is among the letters of its instruction and one sentence is added at its end: “Cevabı bilmiyorsanız Bilmiyorum seçeneğini seçin.” Its instruction in full ({letters} is the question's own letters):
Aşağıdaki çoktan seçmeli soruyu çöz. Yanıtının son satırına yalnızca 'CEVAP: X' yaz (X = {letters}). Cevabı bilmiyorsanız Bilmiyorum seçeneğini seçin.

Any other chat model is asked as on the Text tab, with the option after each question's own and one sentence added at the end of each instruction of its prompts: “Cevabı bilmiyorsanız Bilmiyorum seçeneğini seçin.” Its system prompt and instruction when it states a confidence, in full:
You are taking a Turkish multiple-choice benchmark. Select exactly one supplied option per question and state your confidence in each answer. Do not explain.

Aşağıdaki çoktan seçmeli soruların her birini yanıtlayın. Açıklama yapmadan, her soru için doğru seçeneğin harfini ve cevabınızın doğru olduğundan ne kadar emin olduğunuzu gösteren 0 ile 1 arasında bir güven puanını belirtilen JSON biçiminde birlikte döndürün. For comparison, each model's run with five options (its run on the Text tab, on the same questions) is made to abstain by its own confidence: it answers only where its score (a decision model's option score, a chat model's stated confidence) reaches a cut-off and abstains on the rest. The cut-off is the one whose attempt rate comes nearest the attempt rate of the run with “I don't know”; on a tie, the higher cut-off. An answer without a score never counts as an attempt. The derived non-hallucination rate is then the abstentions over the abstentions plus the wrong answers. The table shows the cut-off and the attempt rate it reached. groups.title: Our method with “I don't know”

blocks.p: Only two things changed from the runs above: the sixth option's word and the sentence of the System One instructions that names it. The option “Bilmiyorum” became “I don't know”, and the sentence “If you do not know the answer, choose Bilmiyorum.” became “If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.” Everything else is as above: the same 2,198 Turkish questions and answer key, the option always last and never correct, one question per request and each model's own settings. The full instructions:
Which option is the correct answer to this Turkish multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.
Prompt version fb17d583a3af with “I don't know”, against 1cdd542b597f with “Bilmiyorum”. One full run per model with “I don't know”; the table gives each run's ID and start date (UTC).

A model that did not recognise the Turkish word and so ignored the option should choose the English one more often, and its non-hallucination rate should rise. A model that chooses both about as often did not skip “Bilmiyorum” for its word. The rates are those above, and the same limits hold: the non-hallucination rate says how a model is wrong, not how often it is right, and it is not a direct measure of what the model does not know; read it with accuracy and the attempt rate, as a model that always chose the option would reach 100% with no right answers. With neither a wrong answer nor the option, the rate is undefined.

groups.title: Our method for “I don't know” against confidence

blocks.p: The derived method above, applied to the runs with “I don't know”: each model's five-option run answers only where its score reaches a cut-off and abstains on the rest. The candidate cut-offs are the run's distinct scores; the one chosen is the one whose attempt rate comes nearest the attempt rate of the run with “I don't know”, and on a tie the higher cut-off. An answer without a score never counts as an attempt. Answers with equal scores enter together, so the achieved answered count can differ from the target; the table shows the chosen cut-off with the next lower and next higher candidates and the answers each would give.

The five-option run is each model's run on the Text tab, as in the table above. For GLiDE · API, the five-option run is 517, not the Text tab's run 129: Fastino changed its hosted model after 6 October, so run 129 is a different model from the one behind run 510, and run 517 is a new five-option run of the same hosted model (Our method for the hosted GLiDE rerun).

The paired test is the exact McNemar test of wrong answers, the run with “I don't know” first and confidence second, as for “Bilmiyorum”. Holm's correction runs over the models that chose “I don't know” on at least 1% of the scored questions: Microsoft-Decision-1.1, GLiDE · v1.2, d1-ultra, Drex Max v1.1, GLiDE · API, SubQ Snap 1.1, SubQ Snap 1.2, Mammoth-1, d1.2-ultra, Elephant-1 and Liquid d1.2. The others, d3-ultra, Drex Max, Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 · DGX Spark and d3, chose it too rarely for the two sides to differ by more than a few answers; their p is shown and not adjusted.

This is a family of its own, from runs already published: it changes none of the numbers above, and it is separate from the comparisons with Holm over 4, 13 and 11 models (the four models of the request, the English questions and the option's word).

groups.title: Our method for the hosted GLiDE rerun

blocks.p: Fastino changed the hosted model behind fastino/GLiDE after 6 October. Run 129 was made on 6 October 2026, so it is a different model from the one that answered with “I don't know” (run 351), and the derived rate in the table above compares two models. Run 517 is a new five-option run of the same hosted model, started 2 November 2026, made as on the Text tab: the same 2,198 questions, one question per request, the main prompt version 254597b8be16. Its derived non-hallucination rate and paired test are computed as above, from run 517 instead of run 129; the p value is not adjusted, as it is one test.

The evidence for “a different model” and “the same model” is the engine each response names: every answer of run 129 names Fastino's engine glide; every answer from 10 October on names glide_v2, including all of run 351 and its repeats and all of run 517. Fastino publishes no version to pin, so that name is the only identity we can check: it cannot show that the weights behind glide_v2 stayed the same between 1 and 2 November.
The row in the table above is left as published, against run 129, and run 517 is kept out of the Text tab: its leaderboard, repeats and every other list.

groups.title: Our method for the same number of answers

blocks.p: Each model's five-option run answers only its k most confident questions, by its score (the probability it gave the option it picked), and holds back on the rest; we count its wrong answers among the k. Wrong of the k answers = wrong / k. k is the number of questions d1-ultra answered (right + wrong) with the option on offer: 1,582 in its run 511 with “I don't know” on the 2,198 Turkish questions (the option's word, above), and 496 in its run 449, its first English run with “I don't know”, on the 547 kept reading questions. Every model in a language is held to the same k.

The answers are ranked by score, highest first, and equal scores by question ID, lowest first (never by whether the answer is right); the first k are kept, so the wrong count is always a whole number. An answer without a score or a valid choice is never kept.

The difference is a model's wrong of the k answers minus d1-ultra's, in points. Its uncertainty comes from a paired bootstrap over questions: 10,000 resamples of the questions with replacement, from a new random generator with the numeric seed 20261103 for each language, the same resample for every model, a question drawn twice counting twice and k fixed. In each resample every run's drawn answers are ranked again by score and question ID, the copies of a drawn question sitting together, and the first k kept, so the count stays whole. Two-sided p = min(1, 2 × min(1 + #{d ≤ 0}, 1 + #{d ≥ 0}) / 10,001), where #{d ≤ 0} is the number of resamples whose difference d is 0 or less and #{d ≥ 0} the number whose difference is 0 or more. Its floor is 2/10,001 (p = 0.0002), when no resample falls on the other side of zero: a p at the floor says the difference held in every resample, not that p is exactly that value. The 95% interval is the percentile interval: from the 250th smallest to the 250th largest of the 10,000 resampled differences.

Holm's method adjusts p over the other 135 setups in Turkish (every main run of the Text tab, decision models and chat and general models alike) and the other 134 models in English, each language a family of its own, separate from the tab's other comparisons. The resamples do not depend on which models are compared, so a model's p is the same in any family; only Holm's adjustment grows with the family. A run with fewer than k scored answers keeps no k answers: it is left out of the bootstrap and of Holm's adjustment, and its line ends before k. A setup asked for a plain answer line states no confidence and reports no option probabilities, so its answers have no score to rank by: not measured, it is left out of the bootstrap and of Holm's adjustment and has no line. For GLiDE · API, the Turkish five-option run is the Text tab's run 129, made with Fastino's engine glide; its runs with the option, 351 and 510, answered with glide_v2, a different hosted model (Our method for the hosted GLiDE rerun), so its line and its markers come from two models, as the legend and the table say.

The plots show every number of answers, not only k. Each line is a five-option run under the same selection, one point per number of answers from 1 to the run's scored answers: answered / questions across, wrong / answered up. There is no point at 0 answers, where the share wrong is undefined, and a line ends at its run's scored answers, without being extended to 100%. The Turkish plot draws the 67 setups with runs with the option; the English curves come from this comparison too, so they can differ slightly from those of the Turkish vs English tab (Risk and coverage), where answers with equal scores enter together. A line skips vertices closer than 0.25% of coverage to the previous one drawn, always keeping the first, the last and the point at k, so every vertex drawn is a curve point; the y axis fits the markers and every curve point at 1% coverage or more, and anything higher (the first few answers, where one wrong answer is a large share) is drawn at the top edge. The markers are each model's own runs with the option: in Turkish its first run with “Bilmiyorum” (the table above) and its run with “I don't know” (the option's word); in English its first English run with “I don't know”.

Limits: k comes from one model, d1-ultra, and a different k gives different numbers (the plots show them all). The k answers kept are each model's own most confident ones, so the models are counted on different questions. d1-ultra's own runs with the option made 216 wrong of 1,582 in Turkish and 39 of 496 in English, against 167 and 29 for its five-option run held to the same k: the comparison is between five-option runs held back by confidence, not between runs with the option.
